text: Both are for fifty thousand dollars over ten years, illustrative numbers, not a real lender's offer. The variable loan's first payment is five hundred ninety-three dollars and fifty-one cents, about forty dollars less a month than the fixed six hundred thirty-three dollars and thirty-eight cents. A fixed rate never changes, so neither does the payment. A variable rate follows a market interest rate, so the rate and the payment rise and fall with it, and nobody knows where it goes next. The head start is the fixed rate minus the variable rate's starting rate; it is negative when the variable rate starts higher. Leah's fixed rate is nine percent and her variable rate starts at seven point five percent, so her head start is one point five points. A point here means one percentage point of interest. Real offers differ, so a head start can be bigger, smaller, zero, or negative.
